He attended high school in the United States, where he was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]. Achiuwa played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]], earning [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|conference player of the year]] honors as a [[freshman]] in the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) in 2020. He was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]] with the 20th overall pick. After his rookie year ended in Miami, he was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] during the 2021 offseason before being traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in 2023. He later returned to the Heat in 2025. He was waived by the Heat after the preseason but signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in November. ==Early life== Achiuwa was born in [[Port Harcourt]], Nigeria, to Nigerian parents of [[Igbo people|Igbo]] descent and grew up mainly playing [[association football|soccer]].{{cite web |last1= Tomes |first1=Evan |title=Precious Achiuwa Interview |url= https://www.nbadraft.net/precious-achiuwa-interview |publisher= | website= NBADraft.net |access-date= July 28, 2019 |date=April 12, 2019}} He started focusing on [[basketball]] while in eighth grade, when he moved to the United States.{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title= Precious Achiuwa, who is on KU's wish list, says 'stay tuned' for weekend decision |url= https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article230369774.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=July 28, 2019 |date=May 14, 2019}} Achiuwa and his family settled in [[Queens|Queens, New York]].{{cite web | url=https://davesjoint.net/2019/11/10/precious-achiuwa-the-journey-from-nigeria-to-the-bronx-to-memphis/ | title=Precious Achiuwa: The Journey from Nigeria to the Bronx to Memphis | date=November 10, 2019 }} As a high school freshman, Achiuwa played basketball for [[Our Saviour Lutheran School]] in [[The Bronx|The Bronx, New York]].{{cite web |last1=Munz |first1= Jason |title=Memphis basketball: A closer look at Precious Achiuwa's unconventional recruitment |url= https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2019/07/08/memphis-basketball-precious-achiuwa-penny-hardaway-tigers-wiseman/1498713001/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=July 28, 2019 |date=July 8, 2019}} For his next two years, he attended [[St. Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]]. The school had a nationally ranked basketball program and he was teammates with several [[NCAA Division I]] recruits.{{cite web |last1=Riedel |first1=Kenny |title=The Slam Dunk skinny on prime-time basketball |url=https://www.capegazette.com/article/slam-dunk-skinny-prime-time-basketball/122650 |website=[[Cape Gazette]] |access-date=July 28, 2019 |date=December 26, 2016}} In his junior season, Achiuwa averaged 18.5 points, 10.5 rebounds, 2.9 blocks, and 2.2 steals per game, leading his team to a 28–2 record. He was named to the [[MaxPreps]] Junior All-American second team.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017–18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/hNi1UD2amUag_PSRxexoDw/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team-.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=April 13, 2018}} Entering his senior year, Achiuwa transferred to [[Montverde Academy]], a prep school in [[Montverde, Florida]] with a successful basketball program that held the No. 1 national ranking in the previous season.{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1= Cam |title=Chosen 25 F Precious Achiuwa transfers to Montverde Academy from St. Benedict's |url= https://usatodayhss.com/2018/chosen-25-f-precious-achiuwa-transfers-to-montverde-academy-from-st-benedicts |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=August 14, 2018}} He led Montverde with 14 points and 7.2 rebounds per game and helped his team reach the semifinals at [[High School Showcase|GEICO High School Nationals]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=GEICO Nationals: No. 4 IMG Academy (Fla.) stages epic comeback to knockoff No. 3 Montverde (Fla.) Academy |url= https://usatodayhss.com/2019/geico-nationals-no-4-img-academy-fla-stages-epic-comeback-to-knockoff-no-3-montverde-fla-academy |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=April 5, 2019}}{{cite web |last1= Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2018–19 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mdbwDYCSa02E7-TpRc5Gmg/maxpreps-2018-19-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm |publisher= MaxPreps |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} Achiuwa earned MaxPreps All-American fifth team, ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA third team, and ''USA Today'' All-USA Florida first team honors.{{cite web |title=2018–19 ALL-USA High School Boys Basketball: Third Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-high-school-boys-basketball-third-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=April 2, |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=April 16, 2019}} On March 27, 2019, he played for the East team in the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], leading all scorers with 22 points.{{cite web |title=Precious Achiuwa Shines at McDonald's All-American Game |url= https://mvasports.com/news/2019/3/28/boys-basketball-precious-achiuwa-shines-at-mcdonalds-all-american-game.aspx |publisher=[[Montverde Academy]] | website= mvasports.com |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=March 28, 2019}} On April 12, Achiuwa joined the World team at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last1= Lundeberg |first1=Bob |title=Nike Hoop Summit 2019: Internet sensation Nico Mannion sure to turn heads for World Team |url= https://www.oregonlive.com/highschoolsports/2019/04/nike-hoop-summit-2019-internet-sensation-nico-mannion-sure-to-turn-heads-for-world-team.html |website=[[The Oregonian]] |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} On May 17, 2019, Achiuwa committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] under head coach [[Penny Hardaway]]. He joined his former [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) teammate, [[Lester Quinones]], and the number one player in the 2019 class, [[James Wiseman]].{{cite web |last1=Fowler |first1=Christian |title=Five-star forward Precious Achiuwa commits to Memphis |url=https://247sports.com/college/memphis/Article/Five-star-forward-Precious-Achiuwa-commits-to-Memphis--131979337/ |publisher= | website= [[247Sports.com]] |access-date=July 29, 2019 |date=May 17, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Precious Achiuwa | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]]/ [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = The Bronx, New York {{cite web|title=Precious Achiuwa - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/224174/precious-achiuwa}} | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 9 | weight = 225 | 40 = | commitdate = May 17, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Memphis 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Memphis Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = memphis | scout s = | espn schoolid = 235 | 247 overall = 9 | rivals overall = 17 | espn overall = 17 | accessdate = May 17, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his debut for Memphis, Achiuwa had 14 points and eight rebounds as the Tigers defeated [[South Carolina State Bulldogs men's basketball|South Carolina State]] 97–64.{{cite news |title=Wiseman has 28 and 11 in winning debut for No. 14 Memphis |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170001 |access-date=November 6, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} Achiuwa scored a season-high 25 points in an 87–86 win over [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] on November 23. As a result, he was named [[American Athletic Conference]] player of the week on November 25.{{cite web|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2019/11/25/memphis-achiuwa-uconns-bouknight-earn-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx |title=Memphis' Achiuwa, UConn's Bouknight Earn Men's Basketball Weekly rebounds in a 77–49 victory over [[Jackson State Tigers basketball|Jackson State]].{{cite web|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2019/12/23/ecus-gardner-memphis-achiuwa-earn-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx |title=ECU's Gardner, Memphis' Achiuwa Earn Men's Basketball Weekly |access-date=April 24, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat (2020–2021)=== Achiuwa was selected with the 20th pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite news|first=Christian|last=Fowler|title=Precious Achiuwa goes No. 20 overall to the Miami Heat|url=https://247sports.com/college/memphis/Article/Memphis-forward-Precious-Achiuwa-goes-No-20-overall-to-the-Miami-Heat-154986334/|work=247 Sports|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=November 18, 2020}} On November 25, 2020, Achiuwa signed his rookie scale contract with the Heat.{{cite web|title=Precious Achiuwa Signs With HEAT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-precious-achiuwa-11-25-20|website=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2020|access-date=November 27, 2020}} He made 61 appearances (including four starts) for Miami during the [[2020–21 NBA season]], averaging 5.0 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Precious Achiuwa 2020-21 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431679/type/nba/year/2021|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Toronto Raptors (2021–2023)=== On August 6, 2021, the [[Toronto Raptors]] acquired Achiuwa and [[Goran Dragić]] from the Heat via a [[sign-and-trade deal]] in exchange for [[Kyle Lowry]].{{cite web|title=HEAT ACQUIRE KYLE LOWRY|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-kyle-lowry|website=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}} On October 20, on his season debut with the Raptors, Achiuwa had eight points, six rebounds, two assists and a steal in 39 minutes of play in a 96–83 loss to the [[2021–22 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|title=Beal has 23, Wizards top Raptors 98-83, spoil Toronto return|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/recap/NBA_20211020_WAS@TOR/|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 20, 2021|access-date=October 20, 2021}} On November 24, Achiuwa made a career-high three 3-pointers while having 17 points, four rebounds, two assists and a steal in a 126–113 win against the [[2021–22 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Gary Trent Jr. keys late rally, Raptors beat Grizzlies|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360096|website=ESPN.com|date=November 24, 2021|access-date=November 24, 2021}} Achiuwa made 55 appearances (including 12 starts) for Toronto during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], recording averages of 9.2 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=Precious Achiuwa 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431679/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He played in 25 games for the Raptors as a reserve in [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24]], averaging 7.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.8 assists. ===New York Knicks (2023–2025)=== On December 30, 2023, Achiuwa was traded alongside [[OG Anunoby]] and [[Malachi Flynn]] to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[RJ Barrett]], [[Immanuel Quickley]], and a second-round draft pick.{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Acquire OG Anunoby, Precious Achiuwa, and Malachi Flynn|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-acquire-og-anunoby-precious-achiuwa-and-malachi-flynn|website=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2023|access-date=January 3, 2024}} He played in 49 games (starting 18) for the Knicks across the remainder of the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], averaging 7.6 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 1.1 assists.{{Cite web|title=Precious Achiuwa 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431679/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On July 30, 2024, Achiuwa re-signed with the Knicks on a one-year, $6 million contract.{{Cite web |date=July 30, 2024 |title=Free agent Precious Achiuwa returns to New York Knicks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40684507/free-agent-precious-achiuwa-returns-new-york-knicks |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=ESPN}} On October 20, the Knicks announced that Achiuwa suffered a strained left hamstring, missing the beginning of the season for 2-to-4 weeks.{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2024 |title=Knicks big man Achiuwa out 2-4 weeks with strained hamstring |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41906479/knicks-big-man-achiuwa-2-4-weeks-strained-hamstring |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=ESPN}} He made 57 appearances (including 10 starts) for New York during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 6.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.0 assists.{{Cite web|title=Precious Achiuwa 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431679/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Sacramento Kings (2025–present)=== On September 25, 2025, Achiuwa signed with the [[Miami Heat]], returning to the franchise for the second time in his career.{{Cite web |title=HEAT SIGN PRECIOUS ACHIUWA |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-precious-achiuwa |access-date=July 8, 2026 |publisher=[[Miami Heat]]}} On October 18, he was waived by the Heat.{{Cite web |title=Heat Waive Achiuwa, Three Others; Convert Young To Two-Way Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/10/heat-waive-precious-achiuwa-three-others.html |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=Hoops Rumors}} Achiuwa signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] on November 4, 2025.{{Cite web |title=Kings Sign Precious Achiuwa {{!}} Sacramento Kings |url=https://kings.com/news/kings-sign-precious-achiuwa |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=kings.com |language=en}} On February 26, 2026, Achiuwa recorded 12 rebounds, four assists, three steals, and a career-high 29 points in a 130–121 victory over the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|title=Achiuwa has career-high 29 points to lead the Kings past the Mavericks, 130-121|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/achiuwa-has-career-high-29-points-to-lead-the-kings-past-the-mavericks-130-121/|access-date=April 19, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On April 1, he logged 28 points, 19 rebounds, one assist, and one block in Sacramento's 123–115 victory over the [[2025–26 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web|title=Kings' Previous Achiuwa: Massive double-double in win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-precious-achiuwa-massive-double-double-in-win/|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} Achiuwa made 73 appearances (including 57 starts) for the Kings during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 10.1 points (a career–high), 6.7 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=Precious Achiuwa 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431679/precious-achiuwa|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On July 7, 2026, Achiuwa re-signed with the Kings on a two-year, $11 million contract.{{Cite web |title=Sacramento Kings Re-Sign Precious Achiuwa
